lines.text: What happens if a fly lays its eggs in your cut?
Most flies want dead flesh. The New World screwworm wants you alive.
It lands on a scrape, and lays up to five hundred eggs along the edge.
The maggots hatch, and burrow into healthy tissue.
Disturb them, and they screw in deeper. That's the name.
In people, it's rare, but real. Nicaragua confirmed thirty human cases in early 2025.
And in August 2025, the United States confirmed its first human case.
A doctor has to remove the larvae. The best defense is simple. Cover open wounds.
Now the fly is back in the US, mostly in animals. Seventy one cases by late October.
The fix sounds crazy. Planes are dropping sterile flies.
A female mates only once. If her mate is sterile, her eggs never hatch.
America beat this fly in 1966. Now it's doing it again.
